purpose: Score independent restoration/conservation systems against the same empirical CREST motif without treating them as proof of the finite theorem.

status_semantics.full: All six motif components have case-grounded support across primary observations, method limits, management targets, and explicit CREST interpretation; this does not mean that one study tested the full chain end to end.
status_semantics.strong_partial_replication: Primary studies directly support several links, but the evidence/state/target chain is assembled across systems or timescales.
status_semantics.direct_end_to_end_test: None of the four cases deliberately compared an old quotient, a response-aware quotient, evidence licensing, and target reportability in one integrated design.

cases.action: remove migration barrier / restore longitudinal passage
evidence_basis: Two Elwha dams blocked access to more than 90% of the watershed before removal.
Post-removal eDNA used 11 species-specific assays and found species-specific recolonization timing and spatial extent.
The presence/nondetection design could report focal passage while providing limited population-dynamics information and not distinguishing some resident/anadromous forms.
Field removal experiments show high invader reduction while native-community responses depend on removal method, invasion history, site degradation, seed-bank sufficiency, and some soil legacies.
Above-ground vegetation can generally reflect seed-bank communities but can also miss response-relevant components; the monitoring mismatch is conditional rather than universal.
Invader-control success can therefore be reportable while native-community recovery remains unresolved in some systems.
After 7-16 years of rewetting, methanogen abundance and composition can approach pristine conditions while methane-production activity remains substrate-limited.
Large-scale tropical rewetting reduced subsidence and supported spontaneous native-tree regrowth while hydrology, subsidence, and vegetation remained distinct measured dimensions.
Hydrological restoration is therefore a reportable target that does not uniquely identify methane-process or multi-attribute recovery; net climate function was not established by the microbial study.

cases.action: reintroduce prescribed fire after long exclusion
cases.partial_reason: The action/history/seed-bank response pieces are strongly supported, but the evidence-state versus reportable-target separation is assembled across studies rather than demonstrated as one integrated monitoring experiment.
evidence_basis: A replicated 16-stand burn experiment showed that fire reintroduction after long exclusion can cause duff-moisture-dependent tree mortality.
Prescribed-fire effects on seed banks can differ from visible above-ground community response.
Ecological condition and fire season can alter seed-bank response.

summary.primary_conclusion: Primary studies across freshwater restoration, invasion management, peatland restoration, and fire ecology are consistent with the qualitative CREST architecture. Intervention responses and method limits are observed; required-state refinement is a CREST interpretation. The repeated projection is stronger than generic response heterogeneity but is not an end-to-end empirical test.
summary.theorem_firewall: No empirical case establishes the arbitrary-m finite no-bound theorem.
